So this is almost kind of a rant but I am genuinely concerned about what is about to happen to a HUGE section of the working population. I got into a plumbing apprenticeship and over a decade later am now making good money plumbing. Enough money to own a home with some land and comfortably be the sole financial provider for a family of 5.
For a while now I have watched as people pump kids full of this nonsense that the only way to get ahead in life is to access it via college. The trades are basically seen as a refuge of the stupid and the lazy. If you can't make it in college, well then there is always the army or the trades. Right now, in the trades (at the very least in sunny WI) we are staring down the barrel of a situation where when the boomers finally retire / die off, there will be nobody to fill those positions in the trades. In my field of expertise, employers are screaming for decent employees. We just can't find any out there. Every company is doing whatever it can to hold on to the workers it has and is trying to find more... There just aren't any. Today, i saw the first 'young' (18 - 21 yrs) apprentice in a LONG time. Usually it is guys from another trade, re-tasking to make more money in another field.
From what I see, we have a BIG issue with perpetuating this horse shit line that only the stupid get into the trades. In my experience, if you are a moron you will wash out real quick. If you are lazy, you won't last long or will spend your days working for a shitty company making chump change. Some of the most switched on people I have ever met have been in the trades. We need to get rid of the idea that you will spend your life hovering above the poverty line as a tradesman... That is crap.
I can tell you this, if a kid joined an apprenticeship at 18 and busted his ass for a few years. Play your cards right and you will be in your early 20s, and the only debts you need have will be a mortgage and a car payment. While you are sitting on the porch of a house you own drinking a beer after a days work, most people your age will be sitting in their parents house for the next 9 years, trying in vain to find work and figure out how they are ever going to pay down the student loans.
